source_english.description: Bicycle Crunch curls the ribs toward the pelvis from a supine bent-knee position.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Brace and curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
Pause without pulling the neck.
Lower the torso slowly to the support.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable curl range and reduce the decline or load before the neck or back loses control.

selected_scene.pose: Supine on mat, pelvis supported, shoulders curled and torso rotated toward LEFT knee. Both hips and knees remain bent around 90 degrees, shins in tabletop; RIGHT nonworking leg stays bent.

selected_scene.supports_and_equipment: Pelvis/lower back on mat, both feet elevated; no apparatus. User explicitly distinguishes bent nonworking leg from raised-legs ID.
selected_scene.movement_trajectory: Opposite elbow approaches opposite knee through controlled trunk curl/rotation; do not extend the other leg in this ID.

source_english.description: A weighted push-up adds external load across the upper back while the body lowers and presses as one rigid plank.
instructions: Place the weight securely across the upper back and start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Brace the core and lower the chest by bending the elbows while keeping the body straight.
Pause just above the floor, then press through the palms to return to the plank.
End the set before the load shifts or the hips sag.
source_english.safety_note: Use a spotter or secure loading method for the weight and stop if it shifts.

source_english.description: Hold one dumbbell at the side, bend the trunk away from it, return upright, then change hands.
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang down by your side.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, slowly bend sideways at the waist towards the opposite side of the dumbbell, lowering the weight as far as you comfortably can.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.

source_english.description: Hold one dumbbell at the side, bend the trunk away from it, return upright, then change hands.
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang down by your side.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, slowly bend sideways at the waist towards the opposite side of the dumbbell, lowering the weight as far as you comfortably can.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

source_english.description: Hold the anchored bar at one shoulder and press it diagonally forward before lowering and changing arms.
instructions: Stand beside the anchored end of a barbell and hold its sleeve at one shoulder with one hand.
Use a split stance and keep the free hand on the hip.
Press the bar diagonally forward until the working elbow is straight.
Lower the sleeve to the shoulder, then change arms.

source_english.description: Nordic hamstring curls lower the body forward from tall kneeling while the ankles stay anchored and the hamstrings resist the descent.
instructions: Kneel tall with the ankles secured and the hips extended.
Brace the abdomen and keep the body in a straight line from knees to head.
Lean forward slowly by resisting with the hamstrings.
Catch yourself with the hands near the floor, then use assistance to return upright.
form_cues: Use the hands only as needed.
common_mistakes: Trying to force a full range without control.
source_english.safety_note: Anchor the ankles securely and use a range you can stop safely with the hands.

attempt_history.name: Muscle Up

source_english.description: Pull from a hang and transition the torso over the bar before pressing to support.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chest is above the bar and your arms are fully flexed.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kip controlled as the chest rises over the bar before the press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: The Calf Extension (Machine) lowers and raises the heels through a deliberate calf stretch and contraction while the feet stay aligned.
instructions: Set up on the machine with the balls of the feet supported and the legs aligned.
Lower the heels slowly to feel a calf stretch.
Press through the big-toe side of the foot to rise as high as controlled.
Pause at the top, then repeat.
common_mistakes: Using the knees to create the motion.
source_english.safety_note: Avoid bouncing at the bottom, especially when the calf or Achilles is stiff.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Adjust the seat of the leverage machine so that your shoulders are aligned with the lever pad.
Place your toes on the lever pad, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or side supports for stability.
Push the lever pad down by extending your ankles, contracting your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position by allowing your heels to rise back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Calf Press (Machine) is seated with the forefeet on a platform, pressing through the ankles to lift the heels.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the knees fit beneath the pad and place the balls of both feet on the platform.
Hold the side handles and lower the heels below the platform edge.
Press through the forefeet to raise the heels as high as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower the heels slowly.
source_english.safety_note: Secure the seat and knee pad before loading the calf press.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: The Chest Fly (Machine) opens and closes the arms around the chest with a soft elbow bend rather than turning the motion into a press.
instructions: Set up on the machine with a soft bend in the elbows and the chest supported as required.
Open the arms only as far as the shoulders remain comfortable.
Bring the hands together by squeezing the chest without changing the elbow angle.
Return slowly to the starting position.
form_cues: Move through the chest, not the wrists.
common_mistakes: Turning the movement into a press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and stop before the shoulder reaches an uncomfortable stretch.

source_english.description: Crunch (Machine) curls the ribs toward the pelvis from a seated machine position.
instructions: Sit against the machine pad with feet secured and hands on the handles.

Return the pad or torso slowly to upright.

Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

instructions: Stand with the sled machine and feet about shoulder-width apart.

Keep knees tracking over the toes and pause at the endpoint.
Drive through the whole foot to stand and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a depth and load that keep the feet, knees, and spine stable.

source_english.description: Hip Abduction (Machine) moves one leg away from the body's midline against machine while the pelvis stays level.
instructions: Set up the machine so the working leg can move away from the midline without rotating the pelvis.
Brace the trunk and move the leg outward through a controlled range.
Pause briefly at the end without leaning away.
Return slowly and complete the planned repetitions on each side.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop before the hip pinches or the pelvis tilts.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Hip Abduction (Machine) moves one leg away from the body's midline against machine while the pelvis stays level.
instructions: Set up the machine so the working leg can move away from the midline without rotating the pelvis.
Brace the trunk and move the leg outward through a controlled range.
Pause briefly at the end without leaning away.
Return slowly and complete the planned repetitions on each side.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop before the hip pinches or the pelvis tilts.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Pull Up (Assisted) pulls from a controlled hang until the chin reaches or clears the bar, then lowers under control.

source_english.description: Pull Up (Assisted) pulls from a controlled hang until the chin reaches or clears the bar, then lowers under control.
instructions: Adjust the assisted pull-up machine and select assistance that allows a controlled full range.
Grip the handles overhand and start with the arms extended.
Pull the body upward until the chin reaches or clears the handles.
Lower slowly until the arms are straight, then repeat.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.

Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Face down on the machine, lift the legs by extending the hips and lower them under control.
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to fit your body and secure your feet in the foot pads.
Lie face down on the machine with your upper body hanging off the edge and your hips resting on the pad.
Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the abdomen on the pad while the legs extend behind the hips.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Face down on the machine, lift the legs by extending the hips and lower them under control.
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to fit your body and secure your feet in the foot pads.
Lie face down on the machine with your upper body hanging off the edge and your hips resting on the pad.
Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the abdomen on the pad while the legs extend behind the hips.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Sit at the calf machine with the forefeet on the platform and raise both heels before lowering them below the start.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are slightly bent and your feet are flat on the footplate.
Place your toes on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the seat for stability.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ankle over the second toe.
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.
source_english.safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.

source_english.description: Sit at the calf machine with the forefeet on the platform and raise both heels before lowering them below the start.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are slightly bent and your feet are flat on the footplate.
Place your toes on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the seat for stability.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ankle over the second toe.
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.
source_english.safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.
